text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Outlawed Islamic Salvation Front leader Abdelkader Hachani walked free from Algiers Serkadji prison on Tuesday after an Algiers criminal court sentenced him to five years in jail. Hachani had spent more than five years in jail pending trial.
- A car bomb exploded on Tuesday in downtown Mascara. There were no casualties from the blast.

- More than 3,000 children suffer from the effects of violence in the Mitidja Plain around Algiers. About 1,700 of them were unable to attend school and hundreds of others had witnessed their parents being slaughtered by "terrorists".
- Secular opposition Rally for Culture and Democracy deputies tried to impose Tamazigh language in the National Assembly (lower house). Arab language is the sole official language in Algeria.

- State-owned oil and gas firm Sonatrach unveils a five-year development programme worth $19 billion. Sonatrach's chief Nazim Zouioueche urges local firms to share in his company's plan through sub-contracts.
